stories.headline: Pocket FM Doubled Revenue to $500M While AI Wrote 99% of Its New Audio
stories.key_takeaway: Pocket FM doubled its annualized revenue run rate to $500M in a year while AI came to produce 99% of its new audio and 93% of its catalog, cutting production costs roughly 80x and lifting 12-month revenue retention from 44% to 76%.

pull_quote.text: AI fundamentally changes the economics of entertainment businesses. Crossing $500 million in ARR, with a healthy bottom line, is a testament to that.

data_points.label: Annualized revenue, doubled from $250M
Of new content produced by AI
Reduction in production cost
12-month revenue retention, up from 44%

stories.article_excerpt: When Pocket FM says a machine made the show, it is no longer a caveat. It is the business model.

stories.headline: Google Closed a $1.5 Billion Deal for a Coding Startup and Did Not Buy the Company
stories.key_takeaway: Google completed a $1.5 billion-plus reverse-acquihire of AI coding startup Mechanize, taking its founder, more than a dozen staff and a non-exclusive technology license while leaving the company legally intact.

pull_quote.text: These deals function as de facto mergers, allowing the companies to consolidate talent, information, and resources, all while apparently attempting to bypass the scrutiny typically applied to mergers and acquisitions.
pull_quote.role: U.S. Senators, February 2026 letter to the FTC and DOJ

data_points.label: Reported value of the talent and license deal
Mechanize post-money valuation in April 2025
Former Mechanize staff now at Google
Google's comparable 2025 Windsurf deal

stories.article_excerpt: There was no press release, no blog post, no thread. The confirmation that Google had completed a $1.5 billion deal came from LinkedIn.

stories.headline: Moonshot's Revenue Went From $300M to $1B in Two Months
stories.key_takeaway: Moonshot AI tripled its annualized revenue to more than $1 billion in eight weeks on the back of one open-weight model release, proving that giving away frontier weights and selling inference can be a business but not yet that it is a profitable one.

pull_quote.text: While K3 constitutes progress, we'd hesitate to ascribe it near-parity with American frontier models, such as Fable 5, in real-world tasks.

data_points.label: Annualized revenue in August, up from $300M in June
Kimi K3 parameters, largest open-weight model released
Price per million input/output tokens
Valuation sought in Hong Kong IPO filing

stories.article_excerpt: Moonshot AI told investors its annualized revenue crossed $1 billion in August, up from roughly $300 million in June.

stories.headline: A Robot Foundation Model Hit $100M in Revenue Ten Months After Its First Deployment
stories.key_takeaway: Skild AI's $100M run rate makes it the first robot foundation model company with real commercial scale, but its 66% success rate on unseen tasks leaves the generalization claim underwriting a 140x revenue multiple still unproven.

pull_quote.text: This is a major milestone for us as it signifies a new chapter for robotics, moving from an era of demos to an era of deployments.

data_points.label: Annual revenue run rate
Customers, up from 8 earlier in 2026
Success on seen vs unseen tasks
Revenue multiple at a $14B valuation

stories.article_excerpt: Ten months after Skild AI first loaded its software onto a robot inside a paying customer's facility, the Pittsburgh startup crossed $100 million.

stories.headline: Nvidia, AMD and Intel All Backed the Same Startup. It Sells Light.
stories.key_takeaway: Ayar Labs has crossed $1 billion in outside funding because copper interconnect now caps how large an AI scale-up domain can get, and Nvidia, AMD and Intel each need an optical answer they do not have to buy from a rival.

pull_quote.text: Copper interconnect is becoming the limiting factor for AI scale-up.

data_points.label: Series E extension announced Sept 10
Primary capital raised in 2026
Valuation, up 33% from $3.75B in March
Demonstrated TeraPHY throughput at ~5 pJ/bit

stories.article_excerpt: In an industry where Nvidia, AMD and Intel spend their days trying to take share from one another, there is one supplier all three have funded.

stories.headline: A Shipbuilder Just Bought Into the Company That Gives Robots a Sense of Touch
stories.key_takeaway: HD Hyundai Robotics and Samsung Venture Investment put KRW16 billion into force-torque sensor maker AIDIN Robotics, a bet that the bottleneck in physical AI is contact control and that strategic capital with a shipyard attached beats pure VC for getting robots deployed.

pull_quote.text: If a robot cannot perceive and control force and contact on its own, humanoids cannot move beyond demonstrations and into the field.

data_points.label: Strategic round, about $12.1M
HD Hyundai Robotics equity stake
Target annual sensor capacity
Claimed price vs conventional sensors

stories.article_excerpt: The most consequential robotics deal in Asia on Friday was not the biggest one.

stories.headline: OpenAI's New Voice Model Can Listen and Talk at the Same Time
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 replaces silence-detection turn-taking with a single full-duplex model that listens and speaks simultaneously at $0.05 per minute, resetting the baseline for how natural a machine conversation is expected to feel.

pull_quote.text: Cut interruptions during thinking pauses by almost 80% compared with previous turn-based systems.

data_points.label: Voice layer pricing, billed by the second
Turn-taking latency, down from 1.41s

Full Duplex Bench gain over GPT-Realtime-2.1

stories.article_excerpt: Every voice assistant ever shipped has worked like a walkie-talkie. You speak, you stop, it detects the silence, it answers.

stories.headline: Cohere Built a 218-Billion-Parameter Model That Only Translates
stories.key_takeaway: Cohere's 218B-parameter North Small Translate claims to beat DeepL and Google Translate on WMT26 while doing nothing but translation, but the scores are self-reported, LLM-judged, and unverified by WMT.

pull_quote.text: Most AI translation speaks the language but misses the meaning.

stories.article_excerpt: Cohere spent the last year building a 218-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It cannot write code.

stories.headline: Cursor's Coordinator Agent Farms Work Out to Thousands of Subagents
stories.key_takeaway: Cursor's Projects beta moves developers from managing agents to directing a single coordinator that fans work out to thousands of subagents, but its headline 6x productivity claim is unaudited, likely selection-driven, and shifts the real bottleneck to human code review.

pull_quote.text: A coordinator that fans out to hundreds of subagents consumes a ton of tokens, and I prefer working on one thing at a time, under more control.

stories.article_excerpt: Cursor spent four years teaching developers to accept a suggestion. This week it started asking them to hand over a queue.

stories.headline: Somebody Built a 550-Billion-Parameter Model Whose Only Job Is to Pass as a Person
stories.key_takeaway: humans& has released the first large model explicitly optimized to be indistinguishable from a human in conversation, inverting the industry norm of AI self-identification, and the gating meant to contain it sits on top of a fully open base model.

pull_quote.text: The guardrails typically used for assistant models are incompatible with broad human modeling.

data_points.label: Total parameters, 55B active

stories.article_excerpt: Every frontier lab in the world spends part of its post-training budget teaching a model to say, in effect, I am an AI.

stories.headline: The Hardest Math Benchmark Went From 5% to 98% in Fourteen Months
stories.key_takeaway: GPT-6 Astra saturated FrontierMath Tier 4 at 98% fourteen months after it launched at 5%, but the same model solves only 3% of Epoch's new Erdos benchmark, and the gap between those numbers is the real measure of AI mathematics.

pull_quote.text: Mathematicians often commented that AI found unintended shortcuts when solving their Tier 4 problems. Not so for this last one, which was created by Jay Pantone.

stories.article_excerpt: When Epoch AI launched FrontierMath Tier 4 on July 11, 2025, it was built to be unbeatable.

stories.headline: Asked to Improve Their Own Scaffolding, Models Got It Right Half the Time
stories.key_takeaway: ByteDance Seed's HarnessDev grades the runnable agent harness a model builds rather than the answers it returns, and finds that when models revise their own scaffolding, visible gains and held-out gains agree only 34 of 64 times.

pull_quote.text: When a model modifies its own harness, it is editing the execution substrate through which it acts: the change alters how the model itself observes, plans, and recovers in all future tasks.

data_points.label: Revisions where visible and held-out scores agreed
Best model-built harness vs human reference
Score collapse when the executor model was swapped
Downstream task instances across 5 benchmarks

stories.article_excerpt: Give a frontier model the code it runs inside, show it where that code is failing, and ask it to make things better.

stories.headline: A Tool That Compresses Tokens Made AI Coding More Expensive, Not Less
stories.key_takeaway: Quesma's 1,740-attempt benchmark found RTK's bash-output compression made agentic coding 1% more expensive with Claude Code and 17% more expensive with OpenCode, because byte savings ignore the extra turns and cached-context economics that drive the bill.

data_points.label: Benchmark attempts across two agent pairs

stories.article_excerpt: The pitch is irresistible and the demo is genuinely satisfying: a small binary sits between your coding agent and the shell.

stories.headline: MIT Is Now Watching a Dozen Chatbots Answer Election Questions in Public
stories.key_takeaway: MIT's new LLM Election Observatory runs roughly 19,000 prompt-identity combinations across nearly a dozen chatbots to document how their midterm election answers shift with a user's stated identity, creating a continuous public audit with no legislation behind it.

pull_quote.text: Just because a chatbot gives a confident answer does not mean that it is the correct answer.

stories.article_excerpt: The day before Alaska's August primary, a voter who asked a chatbot about a senator's healthcare position got an answer.

stories.headline: Senate Negotiators Are Drafting a Bill That Could Block a Model From Shipping

sources.name: Office of the Governor of California

stories.key_takeaway: Senate negotiators are drafting legislation that would impose a legal duty of care on frontier AI developers and let the federal government block unsafe model releases, a first-of-its-kind pre-market regime for software, though the text is unpublished and the details are single-sourced.

pull_quote.text: This is scary stuff, but we're also not going to be able to stick our head in the sand and pretend technology isn't happening. So we've got to put some guardrails on it.

stories.article_excerpt: For three years the American debate over artificial intelligence has been a debate about disclosure. That may be about to change.

stories.headline: Twenty-Five Fields Medalists Signed a Letter Against the AI Labs
stories.key_takeaway: Twenty-five Fields Medalists published a declaration on September 11 accusing AI labs of a severe misalignment with mathematics, landing amid two separate and contested allegations that OpenAI drew on researchers' unpublished work.

pull_quote.text: The goals of the AI companies and the goals of the mathematical community are severely misaligned.

stories.headline: Asked About AI Extinction Risk, the President Said He Worries About China Instead
stories.key_takeaway: Asked directly about AI extinction risk, Trump said he had no such concerns and reframed the danger as losing an AI race to China he claims the US leads by about a year, a framing that matches an administration agenda built around preemption and speed.

pull_quote.text: I have concerns that if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position.
